introduction.definition: The cold-water basin collects water falling from a cooling tower's fill and supplies the circulating-water pumps through a sump and screens. Make-up water replaces evaporation, drift and blowdown; blowdown limits the build-up of dissolved solids; an overflow protects the tower; chemical dosing points add inhibitor and biocide.
introduction.summary: The cold-water basin collects the cooled water falling from a cooling tower's fill and feeds the circulating-water pumps through a sump and screens. Make-up water replaces evaporation, drift and blowdown; blowdown controls the dissolved-solids concentration; an overflow protects against flooding.

temperature.title: The basin holds the coldest water in the loop
temperature.description: Hot return water (e.g. 40 °C) is cooled mainly by evaporation in the fill and rain zone and collects in the basin at the cold-water temperature (e.g. 30 °C; range 10 °C, approach to wet-bulb ≈ 3–5 °C). Evaporation (≈ 0.15 % of flow per °C of range) concentrates the dissolved solids, so blowdown keeps cycles of concentration ≈ 3–6, and make-up = evaporation + drift + blowdown. The sump depth gives the pumps submergence against vortices.

foundation: Reinforced-concrete tank on prepared ground; watertightness test before backfill; allow for buoyancy when empty (groundwater).
alignment: Weirs and launders levelled to a few millimetres so overflow is even; drive/bridge centred and level.
piping: Inlet arranged to spread flow without short-circuiting; sludge lines with flushing points; overflow and drain to a safe place.
commissioning: Fill with clean water, check for leaks; run mechanisms empty and with water; start chemical dosing and tune by jar tests.

routine.task: Check level, conductivity and chemical dosing.

overhaul.task: Drain and clean silt; repair concrete; inspect fill.

lubrication: No routine lubrication on static parts; lubricate valve stems and actuators per maker.

safety: Legionella control; confined space in sumps; slippery surfaces.

video_tutorials.title: Cooling Tower Basin — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Cooling Tower Basin.
Check level, conductivity and chemical dosing.
Clean screens; check make-up valve.
Drain and clean silt; repair concrete; inspect fill.
Watch for scaling: deposits on exchangers. Common cause: too many cycles, no blowdown.
Watch for biological growth / legionella risk: slime, high counts. Common cause: poor biocide control.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
